attempts.prompt:
Create a production-quality transparent native sprite atlas for Titans of War: Civil War, improving the provided reference Confederate soldier action sheet. Reference is for the SAME gray wool shell-jacket, light tan trousers, gray kepi, worn brown leather equipment, rolled blanket and long mid-19th-century percussion rifle-musket with socket bayonet, realistic proportions and subtle daylight. Keep this one recognizable human, equipment and musket consistent in ALL SIX cells. This is an educational strategy-game historical illustration, restrained photographic realism, no cartoon or anime.

Exact atlas layout: TWO equal-width columns and THREE equal-height rows, six full separate figures read left-to-right top-to-bottom. Portrait canvas ratio 2:3. Every cell is square, equal dimensions. Transparent RGBA alpha background, absolutely no floor/background/checkerboard/grid/captions/labels/borders/shadows outside subject. One complete standing soldier in each cell. Camera fixed slightly elevated three-quarter side view, facing directly EAST/right in every cell. No camera or scale changes. Identical cap-to-supporting-sole body height, identical equipment. Both feet remain naturally planted, consistent stance and contact baseline. Leave abundant transparent space above cap and below soles, and around muzzle, bayonet and raised ramrod; nothing clipped or crossing a cell.

Cell 0 top left: ready, rifle held vertical in left hand with butt beside the left boot; right hand relaxed near cartridge pouch.
Cell 1 top right: shouldered firing stance, long musket horizontal toward right, actual butt securely seated into shoulder, cheek resting naturally on stock, correct hands gripping stock and fore-end, elbow plausible. No muzzle flash or smoke, game supplies effects.
Cell 2 middle left: begin loading, rifle vertical with butt at ground beside left boot held securely by left hand; right hand holds a small paper cartridge at lips, opening it.
Cell 3 middle right: charge muzzle, same rifle vertical butt on ground, left hand steadies barrel, right hand holds opened paper cartridge immediately over muzzle in pouring position. No loose powder cloud.
Cell 4 bottom left: ram, same rifle vertical butt on ground, left hand holds it; right hand pushes the separate thin straight steel ramrod into the muzzle, arm raised plausibly. Make barrel and ramrod readable as separate parts. No hand through barrel or duplicated weapon.
Cell 5 bottom right: return to shouldered aim after loading, ramrod returned under barrel, same rifle raised horizontally to right with convincing shoulder-butt and cheek-stock contact. Aim stance very close to Cell1 so the final loading-to-fire change is coherent.

Maintain exact rifle barrel/stock length and bayonet length across rotations and poses, no extra limbs/fingers/weapon, no disembodied parts or rubber elbows. All six equal-cell poses should be useful at small strategy-game scale and convincing close up. Real textile folds, worn wood and steel; sharp clean transparent edges with no red/yellow halo. Preserve natural human detail; do not imitate old cutout fringe. This is a six-pose compressed visual approximation, not an illustrated certified nine-count drill.

Edit this SIX-POSE transparent Confederate soldier atlas. Preserve the identity, realistic uniforms, equipment, precise E/right facing, planted feet and six action roles in their existing TWO columns and THREE rows. Critical correction: ALL SIX WHOLE FIGURES AND THEIR WEAPONS must be about 20% SMALLER at one CONSISTENT SCALE in their own square cells, with at least 32 native pixels of fully transparent space around EVERY part including bayonet and raised ramrod. Row1 ready and fire; row2 tear paper cartridge and charge muzzle; row3 ram barrel and return to shoulder aim. Do not change grid layout. Fix the currently clipped ready bayonet and ramrod: draw their full tips INSIDE the relevant cell with real empty space above; no part crosses between cells, not even a transparent fringe. Put all supporting soles at identical cell-local height, around y=450 of each512cell, cap-to-sole body height approx330pixels acrossallposes. Keep anatomical proportions, consistent weapon length, rifle butt seated on shoulder and cheek-on-stock in horizontal poses. Keep full ramrod visibly aligned into vertical barrel in ram pose. Preserve correct realistic textile and hands. PNG RGBA with genuinely alpha-zero background everywhere except the subjects, absolutely no colored glow, gradient, shadow, floor, text, outlines or grid. Native sheet is1024wide1536high; six512squarecells. Do not crop the existing clipped art; reconstruct complete unclipped weapons and reduce complete subjects consistently.

attempts.prompt:
Refine the supplied transparent six-pose soldier atlas to remove apparent changes of the soldier's height between poses. Keep the same realistic Confederate soldier, gray kepi and jacket, tan trousers, leather equipment, musket with socket bayonet, east facing three-quarter camera, and six actions. Exact canvas 1024 by 1536, two columns and three rows, every cell 512 square. Preserve transparency, no ground/background/shadow/captions/grid.

CRITICAL MATCHED BODY SIZE AND BASELINE: In EVERY cell, the top of the soldier's gray cap must be at cell-local y=112 (within 3 pixels) and the bottom of the supporting boot sole must be at cell-local y=450 (within 3 pixels), giving the SAME 338-pixel human height. All six are the SAME person's skeleton and body proportions. Do not vary the camera, body size, leg length or crouch. Standing natural straight legs with slight knee flexion equal in all poses. Hands may move but shoulders and head height stay constant. Figure centered around cell-local x=230, horizontal aiming rifle extends toward x=465. Every solid visible part including bayonet/ramrod must stay between y=32 and y=470 and x=32 and x=480. Only the weapons can rise above the cap.

0 Ready: musket vertical, butt beside boot; natural equipment.
1 Fire: horizontal rifle with butt firmly seated into shoulder and cheek on stock; right hand at trigger and left under fore-end. No smoke or flash.

5 Shouldered aim: almost identical body pose, musket shoulder contact and cheek contact as cell1, rifle horizontal and ramrod returned. Same cap and sole heights.

Detailed worn wool, wood and steel, photographic historical illustration, clean true-alpha edges, no cartoon. Preserve complete legs and plausible two-hand grips. This is a compressed visual loading sequence, not a certified drill.
